transcript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.
Lorna: Hi Tom. I'm exhausted. I've just finished my work experience week at the hotel in the centre of town.
Tom: Oh how did it go? Did you do a lot?
Lorna: Yeah. It was a very good program actually because they let me work in all the different departments.
Tom: Oh brilliant. So tell me all about it.
Lorna: Well first of all they put me on reception for a morning and I thought oh I know what this is all about.
It'd just be handing out keys and stuff. How wrong I was. In fact they handled loads of different things there.
Special requests, contractors coming in and so on.
Tom: What did you do in the afternoon?
Lorna: Well in the afternoon and evening in fact I was in the hotel restaurant.
There were loads of staff there so it wasn't too exhausting but the manager really wanted
everything done absolutely precisely, really focused on the guests. You weren't allowed to make
any mistakes. I thought it was a bit over the top actually not very enjoyable to work in.
Tom: But they've got a really nice coffee bar at that hotel. Did you get a chance to work in that?
Lorna: Yeah the next morning you're right it is nice. I bet it gets really busy.
It wasn't too bad actually but there's a lot of running around so I was worn out afterwards
and then I had to go to work in the shop. It's interesting to see how shops fit into the overall
hotel culture. I never know who goes in those hotel shops but they must be worth it.
Tom: I suppose they're owned separately from the hotel though.
Lorna: think so anyway there were loads of staff working there but we still couldn't keep up with
the flow of customers because nobody knew where anything was or what they were supposed to be doing.
I was quite relieved when it was over. Then the next day I went to see what the
personal services department did. Fascinating. Yes they seemed to mop up everything else
though and you must have to be a certain sort of person because to handle the requests
and some of the people that make them you have to keep calm and polite and be quite imaginative
to find a way around them and resolve them. Absolutely I couldn't do it. It was beyond me.
So I just sat and watched and listened. Tom: Didn't you have to go with the domestic staff
cleaning at all? Lorna: Oh yes my last day. I was dreading it. I just thought cleaning all those rooms
would be so repetitive and tedious. Actually the girls that do it are really lively and good fun
but by the end of the morning my ears were ringing. The roar of the vacuum cleaners, trolleys going
up and down and the girls shouting at each other. I was amazed the guests didn't complain.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.
Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.
Tom: So what's your assessment overall? Lorna: Well mixed. I mean my dissertation is on a different topic
and I'm not planning to go into the hotel industry but I see it as something that we have to do
to understand certain aspects of this module that we're on.
Tom: Yes I'd like to do something like that actually. I think I'll have a word with the tutor to see if he can fix me up with something similar.
Lorna: The thing is that will take a while. I think sometimes people call the hotel directly
and see if the manager will take them on. Though actually it gets loads of requests so that might not work
that you might be better to do it directly through the careers office. If you've got time to
walk down there. Tom：Yes I might try my tutor first though. Lorna: Well I've got to go now. I've got to prepare
this presentation on my work experience for next week. Tom: Yeah I guess that's part of the deal that
you have to report back. Lorna: My tutor doesn't get everyone to do a presentation so I don't think so.
Apparently he thought my last one was good so I'm more or less doing a demonstration for the class.
Some of them have had very little practice in presenting. By the way what are you going to
do for your assignment this term? Tom: Oh difficult. I've got that video I did of hotel work so I think I'll
use a bit of that to look at the way that business hotels are developing as conference centres.
I really wanted to do something on those big five star resort hotels. I haven't got the time.
Lorna: Oh well good luck.
That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three.
